description.short_caption: CT of the chest showing bilateral cavitary lesions.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the chest demonstrates bilateral lung involvement with multiple cavitary lesions, predominantly in the upper lobes. The cavities have thick walls and are surrounded by areas of ground-glass opacities. The mediastinum and heart are centrally located, and no significant pleural effusion is visible. The findings are suggestive of an infectious or inflammatory process.

description.short_caption: Chest radiograph showing bilateral pulmonary infiltrates.
description.detailed_description: This is a frontal chest radiograph demonstrating bilateral pulmonary infiltrates, predominantly in the lower lung zones. The heart size appears within normal limits, and there is no obvious pleural effusion. The infiltrates are patchy and may suggest an infectious or inflammatory process. The bony structures, including the ribs and spine, appear intact.

Case_09014/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Hematoxylin and eosin stain of lung tissue.

description.short_caption: Hematoxylin and eosin stain of lung tissue showing inflammation and cellular changes.
description.detailed_description: This hematoxylin and eosin-stained section of lung tissue reveals prominent inflammatory infiltrates, including numerous neutrophils and mononuclear cells. The architecture is disrupted, with areas of cellular debris and possible necrosis. The pink eosinophilic background represents extracellular matrix and cytoplasmic components, while the darker purple nuclei indicate dense cellular activity. These findings are consistent with an infectious or inflammatory process in the lung.
visible_findings: inflammatory infiltrates with neutrophils and mononuclear cells
dark purple nuclei indicating cellular activity

Case_09014/figure4.jpg.source_caption: Gomori methenamine silver stain of lung tissue.

description.short_caption: Gomori methenamine silver stain of lung tissue showing fungal elements.
description.detailed_description: This Gomori methenamine silver (GMS) stain highlights numerous darkly stained fungal elements against a green background of lung tissue. The fungal structures appear as small, round to oval forms, some with budding morphology, consistent with yeast forms. The surrounding tissue shows no significant cellular detail due to the staining technique, but the fungal organisms are prominently visualized.

Case_09014/figure5.jpg.source_caption: Modified Giemsa stain of lung tissue.

description.short_caption: Modified Giemsa stain of lung tissue showing intracellular and extracellular organisms.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a modified Giemsa stain of lung tissue. Numerous round to oval organisms are visible, some within host cells and others extracellularly. The organisms stain purple against a lighter background, with some variation in size. The tissue appears infiltrated with inflammatory cells, including macrophages, suggesting an infectious process. The staining highlights the organisms and cellular structures effectively.
visible_findings: light background with contrast to stained elements
